answer: Price identities in sequential time. Consensus takes one answer per account only with a delay-function proof over H(beacon, account, epoch), revealed at epoch start — no precompute, no reuse; the VDF is the protocol's quartz clock, certifying T of per-identity sequential work. Assumes no hardware beats T. Fixed pool R over n accounts: an added identity's marginal gain has a zenith of R(n-k)/(n(n+1)) — under one share, near zero as k→n, like pigment thinned by water — while each account still pays T of rented compute. Linear, honestly: it deters only while that rental tops the marginal gain.
